CMMC_input_biosynthesis_description:
NA; Indole-3-lactic acid (ILA), 3-indoleacrylic acid (IA), and indole-3-propionic acid (IPA) are
produced from the reductive metabolism of Trp.30 Firstly, Trp is reduced to indole-3-pyruvate by aromatic amino acid aminotransferase. Next, indole-3-pyruvate is converted to ILA via
indolelactate dehydrogenase. Then, ILA is catalyzed to IA by phenyllactate dehydratase. In the end, IA is further converted to IPA in the presence of acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (29168502).
CMMC_input_phenotype_associated:
NA; Indole-3-lactic acid is associated with intestinal ischemia/reperfusion injury via positive regulation of YAP and Nrf2 (37072757).
Indole-3-lactic acid, a tryptophan metabolite, was significantly associated with both physical activity and fatigue (35466716). 
Indole-3-lactic acid, a metabolite of tryptophan, secreted by Bifidobacterium longum subspecies infantis is anti-inflammatory in the immature intestine (31945773).

CMMC_input_activity: Both host and microbes are involved in the biotransformation of levodopa (L-DOPA) to dopamine. Levodopa, a medication used for Parkinson disease, must pass the blood-brain barrier (BBB) before it is converted to the neurotransmitter dopamine to be effective. The drug is therefore coadministered with carbidopa, that inhibits peripheral metabolism by aromatic amino acid decarboxylase (AAAD). However, L-DOPA can also be converted to dopamine by a pyridoxal phosphate-dependent tyrosine decarboxylase from Enterococcus faecalis. This decarboxylation can limit drug availability and contribute to side effects.
